item.title: U20 youth training hard ahead of TISA Cup Tournament
item.description: Kolomotu’a’s young men and women are stepping up their preparations for an upcoming local rugby tournament, and were training hard at at Halaano Rugby Field on Friday. Hosted by Kolomotu'a, the TISA Insurance Kolomotu'a Under-20s and Women's XV 2026 Tournament will run for 11 weeks, beginning on August 29, with the finals scheduled for November 7.
item.content:encoded:
Kolomotu’a’s young men and women are stepping up their preparations for an upcoming local rugby tournament, and were training hard at at Halaano Rugby Field on Friday.

Hosted by Kolomotu'a, the TISA Insurance Kolomotu'a Under-20s and Women's XV 2026 Tournament will run for 11 weeks, beginning on August 29, with the finals scheduled for November 7.

Head coach Taliai Taufa said rugby was more than a sport for young people, providing an opportunity to develop skills, confidence and a passion for the game.

“I see the kids playing and it is more than just a sport. They really enjoy playing rugby and we try to teach them the practical skills as well as keeping their interests and passion.”

Taufa said it was important for young players to be encouraged to participate and enjoy the game rather than focusing solely on performance.

“Rugby is not just a sport or a career path, it is also something they can just enjoy. There is no special qualification needed to play rugby,” he said.

The training continued under cloudy and windy conditions yesterday, with players working through drills covering different aspects of rugby.

A young player said rugby had become something she looked forward to each day.

“I get tired but playing beside the other girls is something I enjoy so much. I look forward to our evening trainings every day,” she said.

Coaches said more young women were taking up rugby, with participation growing as traditional perceptions that rugby was primarily a men's sport continued to change.

Women's rugby has become increasingly popular in Tonga, with four women's teams confirmed for this year's competition.

TISA Insurance Kolomotu'a Under-20s and Women's XV 2026

Nine men's teams and four women's teams have been confirmed for the 11 weeks competition. The tournament draw has been completed ahead of the opening round on 29 August.

The men's teams are Marist 'Apifo'ou, Fasi Ma'ufanga, Houmakelikao, Ngele'ia Warlords, Havelu Bulldogs, Hihifo, Toloa Old Boys, Hasini Roosters and Kolomotu'a Eagles.

The women's teams are Kolofo'ou Lioness, Havelu Bulldogs, Hihifo and Kolomotu'a Eagles.

These teams are also holding regular trainings in their villages in preparation for what will be the last rugby tournament of the year on Tongatapu
